summary: Earth Jukebox is an accessible, interactive web application that transforms Earth science visuals and climate data into sound, allowing people, including those with visual impairments, to explore our planet through listening. The project offers two modes: Image Mode, which uses OpenCV to analyse brightness, color, and edge details from Earth images and converts them into musical elements, and NASA Data Mode, which transforms NASA GISS global temperature anomaly data (1880 to present) into melodies using a C major pentatonic scale. It also provides visual representations through warming stripes and interactive charts. Built using Python, Flask, OpenCV, and Tone.js, Earth Jukebox combines science, technology, music, and accessibility to make complex environmental information more engaging and understandable. It promotes inclusive access to Earth science while demonstrating an innovative way to communicate climate change and environmental patterns through data sonification.
details:
Earth Jukebox is an interactive web application that transforms Earth science images and climate data into musical experiences through a technique called data sonification. Its main goal is to make Earth science more accessible, engaging, and inclusive, especially for people who cannot explore maps and scientific visualisations visually.

How It Works

The application provides two interactive modes:

1. Image Mode: Users can select different Earth science scenes, including NASA Earth Information Center images. Using OpenCV, the application analyses image properties such as brightness, color, and edge details. These features are converted into musical parameters such as pitch, tempo, note density, and volume. Tone.js generates the corresponding soundscape in real time. These image features are used for artistic sound generation and are not treated as direct scientific measurements.

2. NASA Data Mode: The application uses NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 annual global temperature anomaly data from 1880 to the present. Each year's temperature anomaly is mapped to a musical note on a C major pentatonic scale, with values from -0.6°C to +1.5°C mapped to notes between C3 and A5. Users can listen to the changing climate pattern while viewing corresponding warming stripes and an interactive chart.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Makes Earth science information accessible through sound.
  • Provides an alternative way for visually impaired people to explore environmental information.
  • Makes climate change data more engaging and easier to understand.
  • Encourages interest in Earth science, music, and technology.
  • Demonstrates how scientific datasets can be communicated through creative methods.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Python: Main programming language and application logic.
  • Flask: Backend web framework.
  • OpenCV: Image processing and feature analysis.
  • Tone.js: Real-time sound and music generation.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript: Frontend design and interactivity.
  • NASA GISS GISTEMP v4: Global temperature anomaly dataset.
  • NASA Earth Information Center / Scientific Visualization Studio: Earth science imagery.
  • GitHub and Render: Source code management and web deployment.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of Earth Jukebox is its ability to turn scientific information into music. Instead of presenting environmental data only through traditional charts, graphs, and maps, it allows users to hear patterns in images and climate records. Combining image processing, real scientific datasets, and musical composition creates an innovative bridge between science and art.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered accessibility, scientific accuracy, usability, creativity, and reliability. We included keyboard navigation, visible focus indicators, descriptive text for scenes, a read-aloud feature, reduced-motion support, and user-controlled audio playback. We also ensured that NASA data sources were properly credited and distinguished artistic image-based sound generation from actual scientific measurements.

Overall, Earth Jukebox aims to create a more inclusive and creative way of experiencing our planet by allowing people to not only see Earth but also hear its story.
